findings.passage: The difference shows in what she picks when advancement and experience pull apart, and in what she does with status once she has it.
findings.problem: The discriminator is framed as choice behavior, but the article shows no case where the two pulled apart and she gave up advancement. At Chapman she kept the lead, the producer credit and the degree, which is doing it all and reads at least as well for Three; the draft itself gives two non-type reasons for staying. What is left is stated preference, quoted selectively. The 2024 line "the material, the people, and the fun" is used. Her 2025 answer to the same question (S30, Numéro Netherlands, reopened 2026-11-10) is left out: "I weigh the director and material, but also where it might take me and who I might get to work with... I'm also such a believer in work begets work." The answer block and FAQ then harden preference into behavior ("Totah picks jobs for 'the fun'"; "Type 7 leads on what she picks...").
findings.acceptance_test: The Why-not-3 section quotes the 2025 "where it might take me" / "work begets work" answer beside the 2024 one. The discriminator sentence, the 60-word answer and both type FAQs present her job criteria as what she says she weighs, not what she picks, unless a sourced instance is added where she passed up a career advantage for experience. The college passage says she gave up nothing professionally to stay. Unused and available in S27: her concrete reasons for taking The Buccaneers (talks with Jakeways, a new genre, a rarely seen character, Scotland).

findings.passage: "I was so afraid to drink because I didn't want anyone to ruin anything," she said on her podcast in April 2023, so she worked the room with props.
findings.problem: The quotation is cut mid-clause and the cut changes her reason. Crooked's transcript (S22, reopened 2026-11-10) reads: "I was so afraid to drink because I didn't want anyone to ruin anything in in my parents house." She stayed sober to guard her parents' house. Trimmed, it reads as self-protection, and the hook's question ("what the control is for") and its answer ("The discipline protects the place where she gets to play") lean on that reading. Two details in the same episode also go uncounted: a co-host says "Josie leaves a trail of drinks throughout the day" unfinished (coffee, milk, wine), so an undrunk glass is partly habit; and a prop cigarette is a way to look like part of the party, which is an image datum the Three case never gets.
findings.acceptance_test: The quote runs to the end of her clause or the sentence paraphrases the parents'-house reason outside the quotation marks. The opening and "Where the wildness goes" no longer present the party restraint as protecting her work; the career motive is attached only to her mother's warning. Claim C24's passage matches the corrected text.

findings.passage: The wildness goes into the work. The discipline protects the place where she gets to play.
findings.problem: A Three predicts this same split: outrageous where it is the product and gets applause (a set, a podcast), controlled where a slip would cost the career. As written the thesis turns any restraint into service of play, so nothing could count against it. The Carrie test repeats the move with "What points to Seven is the means." Improvisation has been her trade tool since stand-up at ten, and by Thornton's account it made a small, disliked part bigger. The same LPM piece (S38) has her saying "Honey, this is my role" and "I got it in the bag." A Three would win the director with her best skill too.
findings.acceptance_test: The article either shows appetite where nothing professional is gained (in the record and unused: S27 "sat several minutes after getting to my destination with my Uber drivers just chatting" and games nights "till our eyes are all closing shut"; S18 talking in a driveway until four in the morning), or says plainly that the on-set/off-set split fits Three equally well. "What points to Seven is the means" is cut or reduced to a lean, with the Three reading of the improvisation stated next to it.

findings.passage: And she deflates her own standing where a Three would be expected to polish it.
findings.problem: This is a stereotype of Three. Self-deprecation is a standard way to manage an image, most of all for a comic. The Three case is built from resume and the two concealments (behavior) while Seven is argued from motive, so the comparison is uneven. The record's motive-level evidence for an image-and-shame reading is left out or spent elsewhere: "I'm embarrassed and ashamed. I'm a poster" (S37), "avoiding the public humiliation really stunted my growth" (S13), room service knowing her name being "truly embarrassing" (S26), and "afraid of my own identity being controversial," which is quoted but never counted. Embarrassment is used only against Eight. "Neither account mentions being admired" also passes over the flashlight she had her brother point at her.
findings.acceptance_test: The Why-not-3 section states the Three motive (worth through being seen as successful, shame at exposure) and weighs her embarrassment and humiliation vocabulary as evidence for it, quoting at least one of the unused lines. The self-deprecation point survives only as a lean, with the image-management reading beside it. The section then says what still separates the two types, or that nothing in the record yet does.

findings.passage: But no single emotion makes a type, and in fourteen years of interviews there is almost no second-guessing or worst-case planning. Discouragement gives her an appetite.
findings.problem: Six is ruled out on the absence of doubt in press interviews. The standard disallows that (absence of anxiety does not rule a Six out) and the evidence record calls it weak (C73). The record holds a Six case this paragraph never weighs: years of not drinking after her mother's worst-case warning; "my parents who are my primary sounding board" (S27); "I was scared to do it because I have the utmost respect for Katherine and our writers," after two castmates told her "You should send this to Katherine" (S26, reopened; the draft drops both and tells the story as "she gets her way with a fib"); three statements about questioning authority (S26, S28, S33); trying to make Wigfield her mentor (S30); "love is safety"; the group "mama"; the store she can't enter alone. The leaves-out section lists several of these without noticing they point at one rival. One Flanagan anecdote cannot carry "Discouragement gives her an appetite," and a counterphobic Six also moves toward a challenge.
findings.acceptance_test: The Six paragraph names this evidence, including the sounding-board line and her stated fear before calling Jakeways (also restored in the Buccaneers anecdote), and gives a Six-versus-Seven discriminator in terms of motive (seeking support and guidance versus reframing and moving to the next option) with her evidence on each side, or says Six remains live. No sentence dismisses Six on what she does not say in interviews. The Type 8 sentence likewise does not treat reported fear as disqualifying a type.

findings.passage: Her dream roles, listed in one breath, are "a period war drama like 1917" and "a Big Mama's House remake."
findings.problem: The list is cut. Wonderland (S24, reopened 2026-11-10): "Randomly, I would love to be in a period war drama like 1917. But at the same time in a Big Mama's House remake or a Julia Ducournau or Ruben Östlund film." The two dropped names are festival-prestige directors (C69 notes this), so "A wish list built for image would point somewhere. Hers has range" is drawn from a trimmed list. Range of ambition also fits a Three.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence gives the full list or says it is partial, and the inference is cut or reduced to what the full list supports. Claim C69's passage matches.

findings.passage: The same reflex shows up as a principle.
findings.problem: The article's own rule sets aside what she says as a trans woman about hiding and freedom, yet her position on how trans and queer stories should be told is counted as a Seven reflex. It is a representation stance many creators share, she credits Jakeways with centering joy on The Buccaneers (C15), and the standard treats a shared act as weak type evidence. The caveat that follows does not undo the framing.
findings.acceptance_test: The paragraph presents this as her stated editorial position and no longer calls it the same reflex as the urgent-care story, or it shows what is specific to her in how she holds it. The pain-handling argument stands without it.

findings.passage: ## What the Seven reading leaves out
findings.problem: The similarity diagnostic tripped on Dominic Fike (2026-10-31, also Type 7). The arguments differ (Fike is tested against Six, Totah against Three), so the reasoning is not recycled. The frame is: the identical sentence "sits in the head triad, the three types organized around fear," this identical H2, and the same order (type answer, "Why not Type N?", leaves-out, closing scene). Fike's triad paragraph goes on to separate Five, Six and Seven. This one does not, which is the gap behind enneagram-05. The other trip pairs ("promotional interviews", "options open") are ordinary vocabulary.
findings.acceptance_test: The H2 gets a heading specific to her, and the triad sentence is rewritten to do work for this case, for example by separating Seven from Six on her evidence.

protected_passages.passage: One limit matters more than the rest. Totah is a transgender woman, and being trans is not evidence of any personality type.
protected_passages.reason: Sets the rule that keeps circumstance out of the typing before any evidence is read, and most of the article holds to it.

protected_passages.passage: Threes, Sevens and Eights all claim a fear of vulnerability, so it settles nothing about type.
protected_passages.reason: Declines to spend a vivid quote on a claim it cannot support. This is the standard the rest of the type argument should meet.

protected_passages.passage: Those are the effects of a circumstance, one that ended, and they do not type her.
protected_passages.reason: Refuses to turn closeted-era anxiety and depression into Six or Four evidence.

protected_passages.passage: The read would weaken if a director or showrunner described her tracking billing, reviews or status, or if her choices after Carrie visibly favored prestige over enjoyment.
protected_passages.reason: A concrete, observable falsifier for the Seven-over-Three call. Keep it whatever else changes in that section.

protected_passages.passage: Someone who calls herself "really down for anything" will not run a mundane errand by herself, and a freedom motive does not predict that.
protected_passages.reason: Leaves unexplained behavior unexplained. No wing, arrow or subtype is used anywhere to patch a contradiction.

assessment: Type 7 is a defensible leading read and I do not recommend a type change, but the case as written does not yet beat its rivals. The declared discriminator is choice behavior the record never shows: she has not been seen giving up advancement for experience, and the college years kept both. Under it sits stated preference, trimmed in three places I reopened: the party quote drops "in my parents house" (S22), the 2025 job criteria with "where it might take me" are omitted (S30), and the dream-role list loses its two prestige directors (S24). The thesis split, wild at work and controlled in life, is what a Three predicts too, and Three is argued from resume while its shame motive goes unweighed. Six is dismissed on what she does not say in interviews, with a real support-and-authority case left in the evidence file. The stronger Seven evidence is elsewhere: how she handles bad feeling (music so she does not "confront my own thoughts," the urgent-care bit, vulnerability she walks around) and appetite off the clock (S27, S18). Rebuilt on those, with Three and Six weighed on motive, medium confidence is the top of what this record supports; if they still do not separate, the article should say the call sits between Seven, Three and Six. Strengths to keep: no wings or arrows, clear limits on self-report, a stated falsifier, and the rule against typing her from being trans, broken only by the joy-in-storytelling paragraph. Not open-case eligible: fourteen years of record. Limits of this review: I reopened S22, S24, S26, S27 and S30; other quotations were checked only against the evidence record. Contested typing confirmed.
